GTA 6: How to Rob ATM Machines

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of GTA 6's main objectives is to make as much money as possible.
  • However, there’s another way to get a good sum of cash that most players may not know about, and that’s robbing ATM machines.
  • It has been revealed that if you are looking for an additional way to earn money in the game, this guide has you covered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of GTA 6's main objectives is to make as much money as possible. There are many ways to do this, such as stealing and selling cars, robbing stores, completing missions, etc.

However, there’s another way to get a good sum of cash that most players may not know about, and that’s robbing ATM machines.

It has been revealed that if you are looking for an additional way to earn money in the game, this guide has you covered. Here’s how to rob ATM machines in GTA VI.

Before you can rob an ATM machine in Grand Theft Auto 6, you must steal it first. To do this, you need two things: a vehicle with a flatbed and the Winch mod attached to it.

Trucks with flatbeds are generally easy to find and acquire by simply stealing one, while the Winch can be added to the vehicle by bringing it to a Mod Shop.

Keep in mind that Mod Shops each specialize in certain services, so not all of them will have a Winch available.

It has been revealed that if you are having trouble finding a Mod Shop that works, make sure to read the shop’s description in the map menu. The description will explain if it specializes in your vehicle.

After attaching a Winch, all you have to do is back it up into the ATM machine to automatically latch it to your vehicle. Next, drive away with the machine attached to rip it out of the building.

With the ATM machine ripped out of the building and attached to your truck, it’s time to get it open so you can claim the money. There are two ways to do this.

First, you can use Sticky Bombs to blow it up, which is the faster way. You can purchase Sticky Bombs from most Ammu-Nation shops across Leonida and they don’t cost much, only costing around 185 dollars.

Recent findings suggest that the other way to open an ATM machine is to continue driving with it attached to the Winch of your vehicle until it breaks and busts open. However, this method isn’t recommended since you need to do a lot of damage to it to open it.

Either way you decide, you will know when an ATM breaks open when dollar signs and blocks of money appear.

Simply put, not all ATM machines hold the same amount of money in GTA VI. From personal experience, each ATM has, on average, rewarded me with 4k to 6k. There have been some that rewarded me with more than that, though, so it really just depends.

Sources indicate that once you claim the cash from the ATM machine, there’s a good chance the money will spray pink paint on Lucia and James. Whether it does or not depends on how far you are in the story.

This is because all money from banks and ATM machines contain Marked Bills, and the paint helps cops track down the thieves who committed the robbery.

In order to deal with the paint and officially steal Marked Bills, you need to complete the mission “Credit Check” during Chapter 3 of the main story. Completing this mission will reward you with a Dye Pack Jammer that makes it possible to claim and spend Marked Bills.

Right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

It has been revealed that I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

Sources indicate that when it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

Sources indicate that there are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

Firstly, Chapter 6 is "progressing well", and the game is now a "structurally complete draft" that can be played from start to finish. In saying this, it will still take a "bit longer" to finish up some other scenes and details:.

"Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.

Sources indicate that as for the recent vote, Queen is officially the winner, taking out 65% of the votes. And the reward is a "stupid scene" from Chapter 6.

Sources indicate that and if this wasn't already enough, there's the Chapter 7 development patch. The team has "only just started", and Fox has read out some of the events and dialogue to the team, but is withholding the rest of the story until they "complete more of the game".

I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.

Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.

Team members who completed their work on Chapter 6 have moved onto Chapter 7 now. Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!

Recent findings suggest that fox ends the latest update, reminding fans how the team has expanded since Chapter 4, but "more and more time is necessary" to keep the game's development going at the "fastest pace possible". The next update will apparently take place when the localization of Chapter 6 is done.

Industry News: GTA 6 “Greatest Artistic Achievement In History,” Says Cyberpunk 2 Director

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (482 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.
  • We don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion.
  • Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.

We don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion. Most studios don't have that kind of change to throw around, because most studios aren't printing money with a game like GTA Online.

Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he mused on Bluesky. "Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.

Industry observers note that "Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he continued. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.".

It's a sentiment echoed by others in the games' industry, like Larian Studios head of publishing Michael Douse, better known by his online moniker - Very AFK.

"Maybe in a world that often feels like it's going to sh*t it is nice for everyone to enjoy a cultural moment together that brings every audience (and every generation) the same excitement, behind something that has turned out to be genuinely brilliant," he posted to Twitter. "Not every game needs to be GTA, and that both makes space for other types of experiences, and the rare moment even more special!".

Naughty Dog game designer Michael Barclay even mentioned that GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child.".

Considering, just three years ago, the industry warned that Baldur's Gate 3 was the game no other developer should try to replicate, given the unbelievable scope and sheer amount of interactivity, recorded dialogue, and branching paths it offered to players, that's one hell of an endorsement.

TheGamer's own Lead News Editor, George Foster, put it bluntly in his GTA 6 review, "we'll never get a game like it again," and frankly, we shouldn't.

Ballooning development budgets are already putting a target on studios' backs, making every single latest release a financial gamble that could mean mass layoffs or even closure, and those high-stakes are only making the industry increasingly risk-averse.

GTA 6 shouldn't set a new bar for other developers to strive for. The unimaginable amount of resources, personnel, and time it took to develop the game is simply unrealistic for other studios. Thankfully, CDPR understands that. Let's just hope the rest of the industry does, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after a one-month delay, we’re finally days away now from the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 of live service. The second season is being revealed today, following weeks of teasers, and some Battlefield Labs testing of the first latest map arriving with the new season.

It’s all going to kick off with a gameplay reveal, which is set to stream live later today.

As we’ve come to expect, the Season 2 reveal will take place via a YouTube premiere. It’s set to kick off live at 8am PT, 11am ET, 4pm GMT on the official Battlefield channel on YouTube - and embedded below. Today’s reveal will also be followed by a more detailed roadmap of Season 2, which will give us a much better idea about the volume and cadence of content we can expect.

Season 2 goes live February 17, kicking off a fresh chapter in the continued conflict between NATO and Pax Armata. The medium-large new map, Contaminated, will be available immediately at the season’s launch. Contaminated takes placed in the mountains of Germany, centered around a once NATO-owned airbase.

VL-7 psychoactive smoke appears to factor majorly into the gameplay of this new season, though we’re waiting to hear more details on that. We can expect new weapons, new gadgets, and the awaited return of the AH-6 Little Bird helicopter.

Look forward to more coverage from us as more details are revealed later today.

#120710. Keeping hold of Tech giant of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO claims – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

Keeping hold of Tech giant of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO claims – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1072 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • Recent findings suggest that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • According to recent reports, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Organization of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Recent findings suggest that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Manufacturer of Heroes provides.

According to recent reports, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell states. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

According to recent reports, just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Industry observers note that anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell indicates. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

In a recent development, relic and new owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Firm of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent patch is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very rapidly.".

I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had prepares to release latest games. Dowdeswell indicates spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a big part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Manufacturer of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

It has been revealed that however, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Tech giant of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a new game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

8 Game Boy JRPGs Still Trapped on Original Hardware

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Game Boy changed lives.
  • In a recent development, with that remarked, you now know my history with the JRPG genre started out humble, and it’s only grown over the years.
  • As much as we look fondly on older console life cycles and libraries, none of them are completely free of strife.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Game Boy changed lives. Some of you reading this might feel like handheld gaming has always been there, but for those of us who grew up with a Game Boy or a Game Boy Color, it was truly something special. I remember sitting on the top of a toy box shelf in my closet, playing Pokémon Gold and Silver Late at night when I was meant to be at school that morning. I’d also rush to finish Pokémon battles because we had just pulled up to school that aforementioned morning and I’d have to get out of the car. But I can’t save right now, Mom, or even pause!

In a recent development, with that remarked, you now know my history with the JRPG genre started out humble, and it’s only grown over the years. Through my line of work, I love to dig up old retro games that I overlooked when I was younger and try them out. With JRPGs, the catalogue is as vast as its age in the industry, which means it had its place on the Game Boy even if you might not recall it. A lot of prominent Game Boy JRPGs made it off the console, but today, I want to look at some games that were left behind.

As much as we look fondly on older console life cycles and libraries, none of them are completely free of strife. There are some interesting developmental stories and struggles from back then, but something that baffles me is that Lufia: The Legend Returns was originally meant to be a PlayStation game. It survived a studio closure to return to the rights of the original developers, and that team rapidly shifted gears and made it for the Game Boy instead. Wild stuff!

According to recent reports, if you’re thinking that shift probably led to some awkward decisions, you’d be right! Lufia: The Legend Returns didn't get the best reception when it came out. It’s a bit confusing for Lufia regulars because puzzles and typical dungeon crawls are replaced with randomized maps that leave a lot to luck above everything else, but the story is well worth picking the game up for.

According to recent reports, the Lufia series is one of the more obscure classic JRPG franchises out there, so if you haven’t played it, it’s worth checking out. Especially since, for all of its flaws, Lufia: The Legend Returns has a unique grid-based battle system and plenty of classic JRPG elements like airships you’ve probably been missing, before Final Fantasy Resonance proved how that kind of stuff just can’t be beat. Like many of the games on this list, Lufia: The Legend Returns can only be enjoyed on original software these days unless you get lucky. It was released on the 3DS Virtual Console a few years back, but unfortunately we all know the fate of the Nintendo 3DS eShop.

Back when the Game Boy was around, a lot of RPGs and adventure games were still trying to find the dividing line between them. One of the games for this little handheld that made that line difficult was Bomberman Quest. The story goes that Bomberman is attacked while flying through space, and when he crashes down on an unknown planet, he finds every single engine of his ship missing. Getting it back requires playing a game that feels like the Zelda Game Boy titles.

According to recent reports, bomberman Quest is a game that I feel like hits a lot of highs, but also hits a lot of lows. Might be why it never caught on. It’s got a true ending waiting for you if you take on all of its challenges, but its also got the most repetitive music. There’s cute NPC interactions between every enemy possible and unique dungeons you don’t see often, like a cloud dungeon. But it runs so slowly. It’s probably why it didn’t catch on, but it’s a fun lost treasure for fans of the old school Bomberman games under Hudson Soft.

Sources indicate that great Greed to me is a good game to look at if you want something historically relevant, fun, and a bit ridiculous at the same time. It’s a game where you get teleported to a strange world where most of the characters are named after food, while also honing in on themes of lobbying and the dangers of pollution. It’s a strange one, but it’s the kind of fun that most games don’t dare to be these days, so I’ll always shout it out when people look for recommendations.

Against the surprising food-themed names, including one named Microwave of all things at the very start, the most wild thing about Great Greed is how it hasn’t caught on sooner. Great Greed reviewed fairly decently back in the ’90s. Considering how so many people don’t know about this game until a list like this highlights it, no one played it despite that. I think it's because no one gave it a try, but Great Greed has been left to biodegrade on the Game Boy all this time.

Pokémon was the most well-known JRPG for the Game Boy. That’s not even up for debate. With a juggernaut like that, naturally a few other companies wanted to try and cash in on something similar. Capcom launched their Pokémon rival Metal Walker in 1999. Despite what this might suggest, Metal Walker is rather creative in execution, and if you ask me, it deserved more spotlight than it got back in the day. It’s as if there was a Pokémon: Special Eevee version from the start. And that Eevee was a robot.

It has been revealed that that’s not even a joke! One of the cool aspects of Metal Walker is that you might only have one robot companion, but this companion can literally upgrade and evolve. You can gather cores you find in towns and dungeons that change the form of your robot on the fly. There’s also another elemental dynamic with different land, sea, and sky forms you can use to your advantage. This sounds a lot like Pokémon, doesn’t it? Well, a lot of critics agreed, and it didn’t exactly drum up interest on shelves because of it. So it’s just been left alone all this time.

Look. I love Mystery Dungeon games. I got into the games, and roguelikes, with Pokémon Mystery Dungeon when I was a kid. Yeah, I know. You saw that coming. Randomized dungeon floors with items to find and plenty of strategy to get to the bottom (or the top depending on the dungeon) is one of my favorite ways to pass the time and challenge myself. There are a lot of Mystery Dungeon games out there, but there’s one I’d like to nominate as an honorable member: Cave Noire for the Game Boy.

Industry observers note that cave Noire is a Japan-only game that was literally Mystery Dungeon before Torneko’s Great Adventure would create Mystery Dungeon as we know it. Like many games that would come later, namely the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon games, you play as an adventurer aiming to join the local guild. To join, you have to be strong enough to get through four randomly generated dungeons with scaling levels. Beat each dungeon six times, and you join the guild and beat the game, but there’s still plenty of dungeons to conquer after that. Its short and sweet size on the Game Boy keeps the game tight and challenging, which is a great retro recommendation for those who want a newer Mystery Dungeon game. Like the Pokémon ones. Sigh.

It has been revealed that if you’ve heard of this game before, you’re likely either thinking that I’ve made a mistake somewhere and added a PS1 game to this list, or you already know this interesting factoid. Yes, Azure Dreams is a PS1 game, but it was also ported to the Game Boy Color of all things. Unlike the developmental shift of Lufia: The Legend Returns, Azure Dreams is a decent port of the PS1 game, even if it had to cut a few features to make it happen. One change you might notice is that there's a more Pokémon-like battle system now, which probably claims a lot about why this game was brought to the Game Boy Color, huh?

Truthfully, Azure Dreams is one impressive GBC game. It features some fantastic sprite work, a very lofty start that matches its upbringing as a PlayStation title, and some in-depth systems you’ll need to learn to navigate and balance. The catch is that the tutorial is pretty heavy-handed, taking up an entire floor of the first dungeon, being explained in dialogue with every step. Oh. Yeah. It’s another game with randomly generated dungeon floors. Seems like Game Boy developers were really ahead of the times with these mechanics.

Ayakashi no Shiro is probably as obscure as they come for Game Boy titles. The title literally means “Castle of Ayakashi,” giving away the game’s simple premise. The Ayakashi are monsters that you’re in charge of defeating. So, you crawl through dungeons, fight ghosts, rats, bats, and more. And that’s it. Literally. Ayakashi no Shiro was considered a game without much depth by those that reviewed it back in Japan, but nowadays, it might be a breath of fresh air for those of us bogged down by more modern, overstimulating games.

In a recent development, out of a lot of games on this list that could probably thrive from some sort of remake or classic release on Nintendo Switch Online or something, Ayakashi no Shiro is probably better off as the retro gem it is now. While a lot of other Game Boy games spawned franchises or at least have a good number of fans, Ayakashi no Shiro is one of the few titles by the now defunct SETA Corporation. As a result, this game’s fate is to haunt the Game Boy’s catalogue like the ghosts within its dungeon walls.

Yes, this really is a vegetable-based JRPG made by Atlus for the Game Boy. Spud’s Adventure is one of my favorite games on the Game Boy just for the humor in that sentence alone. Like Ayakashi no Shiro, there isn’t much to this little portable adventure, so it isn’t one of the most iconic Game Boy games or anything, but seeing Persona-creating Atlus doing something so charming and cute during its humble beginnings is never not surprising for anyone who didn’t know about it already. So I’ll mention it any chance I get.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for a quick and easy Game Boy title to blow dust off of and enjoy for a little while, Spud’s Adventure is the perfect game. As Spud the potato, you’ll traverse a tower to save Princess Mato from her kidnapper. You’ll fight enemies and solve puzzles along the way like every other small adventure game before RPGs were more widely defined. It isn’t too hard, and some of the power-ups are a bit zany. It might not be a game to write home about, but it’s definitely one that I think Atlus’ biggest fans should at least try. You know. For the fact that something this charmingly goofy exists at all. You’ve gotta love it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nioh 3 has received a hot upcoming patch that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest upgrade, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an concern that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into concerns with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an matter that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

In a recent development, hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

In a recent development, cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” indicates game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In a recent development, in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override debuts in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

  • In a recent development, I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

In a recent development, I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Currently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

According to recent reports, my computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

In a recent development, I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is introduced over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

It has been revealed that I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

Industry observers note that I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

Industry observers note that the worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Recent findings suggest that still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

Recent findings suggest that the latest massive content patch has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

In a recent development, this one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big fresh arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Recent findings suggest that varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

It has been revealed that the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Industry observers note that outside of events, there’s a upcoming set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
  • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
  • It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the tech giant's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be confirmed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

According to recent reports, this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Sources indicate that last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

As The Elder Scrolls 5 turns 15, massive mod Beyond Skyrim: Bruma gets a 2.0 patch delivering a new quest, extra dungeons and an "expanded worldspace"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old.
  • "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding newly introduced content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 patch.
  • "The reason for this patch is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 enhancement to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are fresh quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

"You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding newly introduced content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 patch. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

"The reason for this patch is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

As laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several new dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

More clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A new opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

According to recent reports, "All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

According to recent reports, you can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's update.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a fresh playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

8 Red Flags That Lucia Has in GTA 6

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are.
  • He spends the beginning of the game putting in serious work to provide for his girl, and he even fixes up the house to make it a truly livable space.
  • She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are. Both of them go out of their way for each other, and stick together through thick and thin.

Is that really for the best though? Let’s be honest, Jason is a stud. He spends the beginning of the game putting in serious work to provide for his girl, and he even fixes up the house to make it a truly livable space.

What does Lucia do in return? She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her. Let’s face it, she is a walking red flag.

It is vital to stay grounded and to make sure that you don’t want too much at times, and that is something that Lucia just can’t do. She is willing to do anything to make it massive. Her immediate thought after getting out of prison is that she wants to someday be on a yacht.

That is not inherently a bad dream, but the willingness to go above and beyond by breaking the law on multiple accounts and accepting sketchy deals make it a red flag.

Sources indicate that she can work hard, get back on her feet, and provide for her son. She doesn’t need to risk it all to get a lavish lifestyle that may ultimately end up with her back in prison.

Lucia spent time in prison, and she gets out shortly after the start of the game. You would think that Lucia would have learned to avoid crime after spending time in prison. Instead, it is the exact opposite.

She gets out of prison, and her first thought is to commit crimes in order to get money. She could let Jason keep doing his thing, but instead she calls up her friend and makes Jason ask about a job with them so that they can get more money.

Industry observers note that she doesn’t care about staying out of trouble. Instead, she jumps straight back into it. It’s almost like she wants to get caught.

There are a few rules that Lucia must abide by when she gets out of prison, with the most notable of them being that she is under house arrest. This requires her to wear an ankle monitor, and she is only allowed to stray about a half mile away from Jason’s home unless she is working.

While she pays attention to this rule at first, she ignores it the first chance she gets. While her ankle monitor is still on, she goes for a flight with Jason despite him advising her not to.

On top of this, when they have a chance to spend time with Kat and Mattia, she takes the opportunity to have her ankle monitor removed and goes for a night on the town.

There is something to be noted about someone who is willing to fight for what they believe in or rush to the defense of others. However, sometimes this can be a detriment and can hurt a relationship.

Lucia tends to have a very hot-blooded attitude. Meaning, she likes to pick fights when others are in the wrong, and she will defend her opinion until she dies.

If someone claims something salty, Lucia is the first to snap back at them, and while it isn’t always good to stay quiet in every situation, there are times where she needs to learn to breathe, let it out, and move on instead of wanting to fight.

Lucia and Jason are like two sides of the same coin, but one side is focused on control while the other side is focused on chaos, and Lucia is the chaotic side. It is a fun dichotomy in the game, but in a relationship, this chaotic nature can get you killed.

Lucia likes to take the route of violence in most situations. She doesn’t stick to a plan, deciding instead to throw it out and improvise.

It has been revealed that it is this impulsive nature that landed her in jail in the first place while she was separated from Jason, and it is the same chaotic nature that could possibly land both of them in jail if Jason wasn’t around to be a bit more logical. While Lucia gets things done, that type of chaos isn’t always healthy.

Throughout GTA 6, you are wanted, and it is sometimes difficult to get by, but Lucia has the attitude of never giving up, which means that she is willing to fight until she draws her last breath. While this can be good in some circumstances, when you are wanted by the cops, it can be a major downfall.

If this wasn’t a GTA game and someone had that attitude, they would be in a world of hurt when the cops came rolling in. Even when Jason was to the point of wanting to call it in, she refused, and she dictated that they never give up.

Eventually, this is bound to land her in even more hot water than she is already in, and she will only have herself to blame.

In a recent development, lying is sometimes okay, but only when it is because you are trying to hide a gift for someone or maybe you tell a little white lie to your child. It isn’t okay to lie to your partner or the police, both of which Lucia does.

As soon as she gets caught doing something she wasn’t supposed to, which she caused because she refused to listen to Jason, she lied to her parole officer.

In her defense, the parole officer is a jerk and comes off as creepy, but that is still no reason to lie, and to force your partner to lie on your behalf is also wrong, yet for Lucia, this stuff comes naturally.

Sources indicate that there are a lot of people out there who like to party, and that is perfectly fine. They like to have a few drinks, kick back with their friends, and have a good time. Meanwhile, you have the few who are extreme party animals.

In a recent development, they do drugs, hit the liquor hard, and party all night long. That is the type of girl Lucia can be, and that is a massive red flag for a lot of people.

According to recent reports, there are some online who have stated that she is “for the streets” because of her willingness to let it all out and party all night long. As soon as she sees people wasting money on breaking champagne bottles and speeding through Vice City in nice cars, she immediately lets her party animal out of its cage and follows exactly what they do.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

It has been revealed that on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still highlights that the Nioh series continues to grow.

According to recent reports, nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

According to recent reports, as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.

In a recent development, the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one upgrade on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s latest blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In a recent development, in the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of complications should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

It has been revealed that the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo challenges, and other crashes and freezing.

Recent findings suggest that the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more challenges join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

According to recent reports, the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next patch will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported concerns.

Industry observers note that until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

Call Of Duty Maker Activision Files Patent To Make AI NPCs Trash Talk

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (457 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that call of Duty lobbies are synonymous with the worst recesses of the internet, a toxic minefield of abuse and harassment that's better left on mute.
  • Sources indicate that as reported by Dexerto, the patent is called "Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio," and describes using the audio from voice chat to make in-game NPCs sound more realistic.
  • The patent doesn't explicitly mention Call of Duty, but as Activision's leading franchise, it's a safe bet that's where it would end up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that call of Duty lobbies are synonymous with the worst recesses of the internet, a toxic minefield of abuse and harassment that's better left on mute. So, naturally, Activision has filed a patent that would train AI-powered NPCs to talk just like players do.

Sources indicate that as reported by Dexerto, the patent is called "Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio," and describes using the audio from voice chat to make in-game NPCs sound more realistic. It wouldn't copy your voice exactly, but what you say and how you react.

The patent doesn't explicitly mention Call of Duty, but as Activision's leading franchise, it's a safe bet that's where it would end up.

Recent findings suggest that it would do so around 10 seconds before and after a flagged game event, i.e. kills, deaths, and losses, shaping how NPCs behave in the same scenarios. So, if players screamed every time they were trounced by a camper (as they often do), that data would be funneled into an AI model to make the most annoying Terminator.

Sources indicate that the patent doesn't just mention in-game voice chat, however, but Discord and TeamSpeak too, meaning how you mouth off to your friends could be utilized in training AI models by matching timestamps across separate applications. I'm not sure that I want to hear Woods say he banged my mom, but if this patent were to go ahead, that's a disturbing possibility.

Abuse, slurs, bigotry, and the worst habits of anonymous gamers are a hallmark of COD lobbies, and that's why it's best to stay quiet and auto-mute everyone, if not disable voice chat outright. Training NPCs on that is a recipe for disaster, but the patent does note that it would include filters to stop offensive language.

It has been revealed that then again, AI filters have never been particularly effective. Just look at all the awful things people made Fortnite's AI Darth Vader say.

Of course, just because Activision patented this technology doesn't mean it will be implemented in-game.

Not only does the patent fail to consider the ethical quandaries of AI-generated dialogue and how it squeezes actors out of the creative process entirely — something that SAG-Aftra has repeatedly taken aim at over the years — but it makes no mention of asking for permission to use voice chat audio or the implications of using private conversations from third-party apps.

Reactive NPC dialogue is certainly an interesting idea, but using AI as a shortcut to shortchange actors and risking a breach of player privacy is one of the worst ways you could go about it. Maybe we should leave this patent in the filing cabinet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a latest Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC looks. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That said, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game presently looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:.

According to recent reports, as you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

In a recent development, rounding out the expansion are new enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an update alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

As much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.
