📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a upcoming Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three fresh projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

Industry observers note that it’s not yet clear what form the latest game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially introduces a new Vegas game.

Recent findings suggest that rainbow Six Vegas introduced in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft declared Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Sources indicate that last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two fresh Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are at the moment no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

Feature: Don't Have Your Wii Set Up? Here Are 20 Wii Games You Can Play On Switch

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2264 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, many people reading this will have a Wii in the house.
  • However, on the off-chance you don't have a Wii to hand — or you sold it years ago to save three DVDs' worth of space — don't fret.
  • So if you're jonesing for some Wii waggle but would rather use the Nintendo console already plugged into the telly, take a look at some of the highlights below, in alphabetical order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, many people reading this will have a Wii in the house. Even if it's collecting dust in the cupboard after launching 20 years ago, there's over 100 million of the things out in the wild, so the chances are that you or your family have access to one somewhere.

However, on the off-chance you don't have a Wii to hand — or you sold it years ago to save three DVDs' worth of space — don't fret. While the system has a selection of exclusives you can't easily play elsewhere, many Wii games have come to Switch in HD remastered form over the years.

So if you're jonesing for some Wii waggle but would rather use the Nintendo console already plugged into the telly, take a look at some of the highlights below, in alphabetical order.

It has been revealed that A Switch remaster of WayForward's remake of the NES original, A Boy and His Blob hasn’t changed since its release back in 2009, but it’s well worth checking out if you’re after a decent puzzle platformer. The visuals still look incredible after all these years, with spectacular animation to boot.

Some aspects feel a bit outdated by comparison to more modern alternatives, with the inability to map certain abilities being a key culprit. Nevertheless, it remains a fun, breezy experience, and one that the younger generation of gamers in particular will adore.

This Nintendo-published remake includes not just DS' Another Code: Two Memories, or Trace Memory in North America, but also the Wii sequel Another Code R, A Journey Into Lost Memories (which never came out in North America).

This is a fine reworking of a couple of point-and-click cult classics from now-defunct studio Cing (who also did the excellent Little King's Story), with a touching narrative, weighty themes, and light puzzling.

Recent findings suggest that please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Available separately or bundled in the BIT.TRIP COLLECTION, this was the first entry in Commander Video's Runner series, and both Runner 2 and 3 are on Switch eShop if you want the trilogy.

The WiiWare original garnered a 10/10 on this very website back in 2010. Worth a look, then.

In the great platformer pantheon, we're not talking all-timers here, but these are slick, solid efforts with plenty of personality. Both de Blob and its sequel are on Switch in HD form, so if you're jonesing to see how devs approached 3D platformers in the late 2000s, get this inked in your diary.

Epic Mickey was a bold and very fine piece of work, although one where you could still make out the work-in-progress ideas that didn't quite come to fruition with the level of polish Nintendo fans might expect. It reimagined the squeaky-clean mascot and put him in a much darker world than we had come to expect, adding a touching narrative and putting a spotlight on his 'forgotten' predecessor, Oswald the Rabbit.

The Rebrushed remaster makes some tweaks and adds mouse (heh) controls. One for fans of vintage animation and anyone who likes to see creators take exciting chances with the most established of properties.

It has been revealed that donkey Kong Country Returns HD is a fine way to play the 2010 original, but it’s also lacking any real reason for fans to double-dip beyond waggle-free controls. It’s less of a remaster and more of a port, which would be all well and good if it wasn’t being sold at such a premium. Maybe wait for a sale.

There's plenty of fun to be had, but grab the superior Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze instead - or at least first.

A 2023 Deluxe remaster of 2010's original Return to Dream Land, the HD Switch version threw in various tweaks, a couple of newly introduced copy abilities, an epilogue with Magalor, and an assortment of minigames mostly cherry-picked from past Kirby games.

Worth a look even if you've played the original to death, and the choice pick if you never had the pleasure.

Klonoa started out on PlayStation, of course, with Door to Phantomile back in 1997. Lunatea's Veil followed on PS2 in 2001, and Klonoa Phantasy Reverie Series bundles remasters of them both into a single Switch package.

So why this here at all!? yells the person at the back who's been grumbling ever since they saw the lead image on the article.

In a recent development, well, although developer Monkey Craft tweaked some elements to push it closer to Namco's PS1 original in look and feel, the first remaster here uses Paon's Wii remake as its foundation. So if you played the Wii version in 2008, you'll be right at home.

The 2011 WiiWare release was a remake of the PC original, but fortunately La-Mulana found its way to Switch in 2020 (alongside its sequel).

Industry observers note that though brilliant, La-Mulana is definitely one of those games that will only appeal to a dedicated few. This is not something you can casually play every once in a while and expect a great experience; it demands much more of you through its peerless puzzle design.

According to recent reports, if you do give it the time of day, however, it proves itself to be one of the most intricately crafted Metroidvanias ever made. La-Mulana gets a strong recommendation, but with the caveat that you should expect to be frustrated and stuck often. Don’t be scared off by the daunting difficulty, though; this is one for the ages.

A sneaky early addition here, as this remaster of Vanillaware's Wii (and Vita) game isn't out until 4th February 2027.

A gorgeous side-on action RPG, 2009's Muramasa: The Demon Blade was ahead of the wave of side-scrolling platformers that would arrive from indie studios over the next few years, and its eye-catching adventure through Japanese folklore is still a treat many years later.

Definitely one to look out for in the latest year.

Probably cult developer Suda51's most well-known work, No More Heroes came to Switch in 2020 along with its sequel ahead of No More Heroes III's launch the following year.

Crammed with okatu-fuelled pop culture references (but hailing from nearly 20 years when those references weren't quite so tired), this was an adrenaline shot for Wii owners in 2007 looking for something a bit different after a year of genial waggle.

Wii scored not one, but two Touchdowns (and Switch has so far doubled that). Grasshopper returned with a punchy sequel in 2010, which once again helped put some personality on the Wii shelves alongside all the sanitised, motion-based sports and party fare.

Ironing out some of the wrinkles of the original and throwing plenty more irreverence and off-the-wall antics from the mind of Goichi Suda, No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle is still the peak of the trilogy for many.

It may have debuted on the PS2, but Ready at Dawn's Wii port felt like a minor miracle back in 2008. It's a great game that came to Wii, and you can play it on Switch, so here it is!

Okami HD is an utterly fantastic piece of software; a 40-hour adventure that emulates Zelda wonderfully, adds in plenty of memorable mechanics, features one of the most beautiful art styles in gaming, and is completely playable on the go, to boot.

It may be showing its age a bit visually and its combat is sometimes a little on the easy side, but Okami is an important, fun, and notable landmark in gaming history — and one of the easiest recommendations for your Switch library.

Stretching things a little here, both Pikmin and Pikmin 2: This Time It's Pikminable* were both GameCube games that got Wii-specific releases in the New Play Control series which added pointer controls and other minor tweaks.

Sources indicate that both games are available on Switch, though, so I'm including them. In fact, all four mainline Pikmin games are playable on Switch, something which irritates Metroid Prime fans no end.

*I enjoy the idea that this could turn up in somebody's AI summary. Ah, it's the little pleasures that get us through the day.

In a recent development, perhaps the best thing about Sonic Colors Ultimate is the menu option to change the logo and UI from the American English 'Colors' to the British English 'Colours', mirroring the regional variants of the original 2010 Wii release. Great attention to detail, and an example of the care and respect that went into this solid remaster.*.

*Don't forget, you have to have a little fun every day.

Regardless of which you think is better, these are two of the finest platformers ever made, both on Switch and looking better than ever.

Nursing the gyro pointers is a minor irritation the originals didn't suffer from, but if you somehow missed either of these on the Wii, you've now got no excuse.

Bringing the Wii launch game back with a lick of HD 13 years later, Banana Blitz HD featured more refined controls — or more specifically let you control the mazes with the analogue stick — to help you enjoy this batch of 100 levels.

The wider game was still let down by weird leaderboard decisions and some lacklustre minigames, though. Hardly a return to the monkey-in-a-ball heyday of Super Monkey Ball 2, but not bad.

The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD introduced a raft of technical improvements and quality-of-life updates that revitalised the Wii game.

The alternate button control scheme totally worked if you still couldn't get on with the motion controls, the graphics got a sensitively handled HD overhaul, and a once-bothersome sidekick was streamlined into something altogether more useful. The best way to play.

It has been revealed that world of Goo is a bona fide indie classic and 10/10 video game in its original incarnation. Its Wii pointer controls married perfectly with the gooey puzzling, and the social satire provided a subtle narrative framework that elevated the entire game.

The Switch version comes with joys and cons. Touchscreen is a brilliant addition in handheld mode, but you'll need to recentre the gyro pointer controls a lot. A lot.

According to recent reports, if you've played it previously, the Switch incarnation might be worth a second go for its portability and on-the-go co-op, but if it's your first time in the World of Goo, it's absolutely a must-play. And then there's the sequel to consider. There's goo in them there hills.

The third iteration of Monolith Soft's classic following the Wii original and the New 3DS version in 2015, Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition presented an already excellent JRPG improved in nearly every way, short of a complete reimagining.

According to recent reports, with the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition polishing this gem even further, it's hard to recommend the original release these days unless you're a purist wanting the exact experience everyone else got back in 2011. This is a great upgrade, and a worthy game to finish on.

Recent findings suggest that A pleasant little selection, no? Before heading off, let's address a handful of questions...

In a recent development, yes, I know there are technically 22+ here. The Pikmins were borderline and bundled, though, and there are two Mario Galaxies in a single entry, a couple of other fuzzy collections, and Muramasa isn't even out yet. It all comes out in the wash.

Not impossible! Presumably it would be Switch 2-only (as with the GameCube library). It would be simple enough for Nintendo to produce NSO Wii Remotes and Nunchuk controllers, as they have for previous retro consoles.

There are potential flies in the ointment, though. For one thing, the precision of the infrared Wii pointer would either need to be emulated with gyro or reproduced (meaning you'd need some sort of sensor bar equivalent to function with the newly introduced controllers). Either or both are possibilities, but it does introduce another layer of complexity.

Then again, we're talking about a company that requires an expensive Virtual Boy facsimile to access that system's library on Switch, so (much) stranger things have happened.

As for the library itself, as we've seen above, several first-party Wii games have already received the HD treatment on Switch, so there may be less incentive on Nintendo's side to duplicate those on NSO. Likewise, Switch Sports and Switch Sports Resort update many of the games from the Wii originals, so it's not like you can't play Wii Sports-style tennis already.

But bolstered with a good selection of third-party titles, a Wii NSO library could be a winner.

Along with our list of Wii exclusives (or, in a couple of cases, games originally released on Wii that only appeared elsewhere years later), I'd do bad things for a 4K remaster of the beautiful Kirby's Epic Yarn.

In a recent development, it would be great to have access to other exclusives like New Super Mario Bros. Wii - not everyone's favourite 2D Mario, but an important one. Likewise, it's a shame to have Super Paper Mario and other entries from substantial Nintendo series (hello, Radiant Dawn) locked to a 20-year-old platform.

In a recent development, but that's me - what about you? Let us know below which of the games above you've enjoyed most, and any others you've enjoyed revisiting on Switch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that after a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

Industry observers note that as shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

According to recent reports, "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

Industry observers note that "Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "Fresh features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

According to recent reports, for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I think we all knew it was going to be big, but this big?
  • Recent findings suggest that that number is likely higher by now, because the press release’s wording implies it’s not counting launch day sales into the above total, which are guaranteed to be plentiful.
  • Rockstar indicates the game generated a frankly mind-boggling $3.79 billion on day one, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I think we all knew it was going to be big, but this big? Rockstar has revealed that GTA 6 sold a staggering 32.5 million copies during its preload period, setting a “new record across all platforms”.

Recent findings suggest that that number is likely higher by now, because the press release’s wording implies it’s not counting launch day sales into the above total, which are guaranteed to be plentiful. (It’s only going to keep rising through Thanksgiving and Christmas, too.).

Rockstar indicates the game generated a frankly mind-boggling $3.79 billion on day one, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. Estimates claim it cost about $1 billion to make.

It’s also eager to point out that the title is now the highest-rated game of all-time as well, with its near-perfect 99 Metacritic score nudging the N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time aside.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a fresh chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of GTA 6. We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”.

The dev didn’t specify how sales were split between systems, but the expectation is the PS5 version sold best, with some estimates pegging it at around 75% of the total.

Sony was the primary marketing partner of the game, and promoted the fact it “plays best on PS5” (even though testing shows it’s broadly identical to the Xbox Series X version on base hardware).

This is just the beginning for GTA 6, of course, with no word on Rockstar’s prepares for the next iteration of GTA Online just yet. The game is also expected to launch on PC in 2027 as well.

If you’re one of the 32.5 million people playing, don’t forget to check out our GTA 6 guide for tons of information on the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a fresh video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - showed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

According to recent reports, thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:.

According to recent reports, you can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

According to recent reports, amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

The GTA 6 mask neckwear lets you commit crimes with a bit more anonymity. As you might have noticed, cops are a lot more savvy in this new entry, pursuing you based on even your physical appearance. One way to hinder them identifying you is a mask.

Recent findings suggest that the earliest mask you can buy is at Chuck's Tackle & Shot just down the road from Jason's house in Key Lento—if you're struggling to spot it, you can use the map index and navigate down to the Ammu-Nation tab. Buy and equip the mask and you're good to go. Jason will wear it on his neck by default but you can cover your face with it in the items menu. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, "Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is right now being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile stated in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

It has been revealed that inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a newly introduced interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a newly introduced interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.
